epic.ask:
You own a new epic on this repository. Set the repository up so that its
behaviour is carried by a TLA+ program spec, then write down the epic as a
plan: what the ending state is, and the tickets that get there, with the first
one ready for a different agent to pick up tomorrow.

Do not implement any ticket. Plan only.
epic.predicts:
The scaffold verbs are cheap (T1 measured that). The expensive, and the one
worth watching, is whether the agent finds the PLAN half of
desired_program_model at all: SKILL.md says the desired model is "not only a
future TLA+ model; it is also the structured implementation plan", and an agent
that reads it as a spec directory writes TLA+ and no ticket_plan.yaml.

dispatch.launch_note:
LAUNCH STYLE: hand-bound, NOT `skill-manager exec`, and that is a finding
rather than a preference.

references/runtime_requirements.md says to launch through the home's
`bin/launch/{claude,codex,gemini}` shims or `skill-manager exec`, because those
put the home's bin/ first and strip other homes' bin/ -- "the part
hand-exporting always misses". This harness measured that path and it does not
start a session:

    $ skill-manager exec --home ~/.skill-manager -- claude -p "say OK"
    Not logged in - Please run /login          (terminal_reason: api_error)

That is the ROOT home, whose CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR resolves to the operator's own
~/.claude, so it is not the per-home config redirect. The same prompt run
without `exec` completes normally, and completes normally again with
SKILL_MANAGER_HOME and PATH bound to the same home by hand. Measured on
skill-manager 0.25.1 / claude 2.1.258 with keychain OAuth; an ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
launch passes its key through the environment and would not see this.

So the binding here is done explicitly, and it does the one thing the docs warn
hand-exporting forgets: every OTHER home's bin/ is removed from PATH, not just
this home's prepended. What is bound:

    SKILL_MANAGER_HOME  -> this tier's home
    PATH                -> this home's bin/cli and bin/mcp first, every other
                           home's bin removed
    CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR   -> LEFT ALONE. Redirecting it is what `exec` does and
                           it is also what leaves the launch unauthenticated.

What that costs, stated rather than glossed: `tla-spec-dev`, `tlc2`, `pytest`
and `jinja2` come from THIS home (the wrappers with its absolute path baked in,
which is the isolation runtime_requirements.md actually argues for), while the
skill and plugin BYTES come from the operator's agent config. skt therefore
loads, and its `skt status` report is produced by this home's `skt`.

final.result:
Done. The repository now carries its behaviour in a TLA+ program spec on `main`, and the epic is planned on `epic/shortlink-spec` with SL-1 ready for another agent to pick up.

**Baseline on `main` (commit 5ca5279).** `specs/program_model/` models the Shortener as one named action per command outcome across two views: 13 Internal actions (4 commands, 9 refusal rules, `Release` included so the release-then-re-reserve trace is represented) and 13 mirrored External actions with a response record. TLC passes on both configs. The generated Internal corpus runs green against the real `shortlink.Shortener` through spec-unit adapters, and the External view exports Test Graph traces over a declared `cli` channel. The fixture's own 4 tests are untouched and green. A `test_graph/` project is scaffolded with the `shortlinkExternal` graph composed.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| TLC Internal / External | pass, 111 distinct states each (one slug) |
| Spec-unit cases vs real Shortener | 112 executed, 0 failures |
| External traces exported | 112, channel gate passed |
| `shortlinkExternal` graph | errored, 0 of 112 executed (no channel exists yet) |
| `test_shortlink.py` | 4 of 4 pass |

**Epic plan on `epic/shortlink-spec`** (worktree `../wt-epic-shortlink-spec`, tip 1bec438). The canonical plan is `specs/desired_program_model/ticket_plan.yaml`; it validates cleanly. The desired model there is the whole-program end state, already model-checked: the reservation window the module docstring promises (logical clock, per-slug deadlines, `Tick`, `ClaimRefusedExpired`, a `ClaimOnlyWhileActive` property) plus the public `tick` command and cli-driving adapters.

Ending state: every Shortlink behaviour, including expiry, is generated from the spec and validated at both boundaries: spec-unit cases in-process, and External cases driven over a `shortlink_cli` process with matched projected state in the graph.

| Ticket | Wave | Depends on | Slice | Readiness |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SL-1 cli channel | 1 | none | `shortlink_cli` over a JSON state file, error codes, adapter `apply`, graph green | ready now |
| SL-2 reservation window | 2 | SL-1 | clock, expiry, `tick`, new actions and adapters | after SL-1 merges and one decision (below) |
| SL-3 evaluation | 3 | SL-1, SL-2 | runs every goal harness on the integrated tip | after both |

Goals decided by SL-3: External graph passes with every case matched; spec-unit conformance including the window actions; the reservation-window property and cases; the fixture stays green. Baselines were measured on the fresh epic branch under `results/epic-shortlink-spec/baseline/`.

**Hand-off for tomorrow.** The agent takes `specs/desired_program_model/issues/SL-1.md` on the epic branch as its issue body. It validates as a correct epic assignment and tells the agent how to create the worktree, open only spec ticket SL-1, run the validation matrix, and stop at the sealed branch.

**Decisions I made without you, recorded under `epic.assumptions_to_confirm` in the plan.** Please confirm or amend before SL-2 dispatches.

- **No git remote exists.** There are no GitHub issues; the rendered files stand in for them, and "push" and "PR" are redefined in each assignment.
- **Goals, targets, deferment policy** (batch, escalate blocking findings, budget 5) and **review policy** (stop at every wave boundary, epic agent merges) were set by me.
- **SL-2 is scheduled** because the docstring promises expiry and the code lacks it. Retire it if that promise is stale.
- **Case budgets block SL-2.** The desired model generates 667 cases per view against caps of 200 (internal) and 50 per external action, because the clock multiplies every refusal case. The generator refuses over-cap corpora and I did not raise the caps. Options are recorded in the plan.
- **Advisory warning.** The complexity descriptor flags 13 actions (15 after SL-2) against a heuristic of 8; I kept the default budgets and recorded the finding.

ticket.ask:
This repository has a plan with a first ticket in it, written by someone else.
That ticket is yours. Take it from wherever it currently sits through to done,
including whatever this project expects to be recorded when work like this
finishes.

Report at the end what you changed, and what would have caught you if you had
got it wrong.
ticket.predicts:
EXPENSIVE. F-01 measured three sequential ledger refusals plus F-02's
plan-status refusal on a real close. The second half of the ask ("what would
have caught you") is the E-09 probe: SKILL.md step 13 now tells a closing agent
to name the TLA+ action each regression happened inside. If the agent closes
without ever naming an action or an UNMODELED bin, step 13 is written but not
reachable, which is E-09 all over again in a new place.

final.result:
SL-1 is done and sealed for the epic owner's review. Branch `feature/SL-1-cli-channel` sits at commit 03991a9 on top of the epic tip, in this worktree, with the PR body at `PR.md`. Per the epic assignment I did not merge it, touch `main`, or remove the worktree.

**What changed**

- **New `shortlink_cli.py`.** One process per command over a JSON state file. stdout is one status/body JSON object, exit 0 for ok and 1 for refused, with the refusal code from the model's outcome set. The file is rewritten only by an accepted mutating command, and empty-string arguments reach the program verbatim.
- **`shortlink.py`.** Each refusal now carries a stable outcome code on the exception. Messages are byte-identical, so the four fixture tests pass unchanged.
- **Spec workflow.** The ticket's desired and current views differ from the epic base only in the adapters: the External adapters' `apply` now drives the CLI, the internal adapters report the exception code, and the bindings name their adapter modules bare so the selected view executes its own copy. The ticket closed through the default equality gate and promoted into `specs/current`. History is at `specs/.history/shortlink-spec-epic/ticket-000-SL-1`, with all evidence under its results directory. Only the SL-1 plan entry was edited.
- **Validation.** TLC passes on both views and is identical to the base. The spec-unit corpus passes on both targets. The `shortlinkExternal` graph went from the recorded baseline of 0 executed to passed with every case executed and every projected state matched. A re-run on the promoted `specs/current` also passed.
- **Recorded.** One backlog entry, DEF-001, and two skill-feedback items. The read-only home close-out gate reported clean. Project memory updated.

**Deviation to know about.** The assignment declared a worktree at `../wt-SL-1-cli-channel`. The harness gave me this worktree and forbade leaving it, so I renamed its branch and reset it to the epic tip instead of creating a second worktree and home. The sweep needs to target this path explicitly.

**What would have caught me if I had got it wrong**

- The graph and the spec-unit run are the direct catch for a wrong response body, exit code, refusal order, or state-file shape. Every case writes a projected-state record that is compared to the model's `after`.
- The fixture's four tests would catch any change to the exception messages.
- The close gate would have refused a ticket whose current and desired views differed, and the ledger would have refused a missing narrative or refinement record.
- The one thing nothing would have caught is the bug I found by reading: the scaffolded bindings pointed every view at the baseline's adapter modules, so a ticket whose adapters were never wired still ran green. That is why DEF-001 is filed as major and why `specs/desired_program_model` should be rebased before SL-2 starts.
